FR-001.title: The system MUST return fully detached public live-state projections, including every nested terminal-transition value, while preserving nil and empty-value semantics.

FR-002.title: The system MUST expose stable structured identities for known control-command failure categories and MUST classify wrapped failures without inspecting human-readable message text.

FR-003.title: Tunnel start, stop, and reconfiguration operations MUST handle repeated in-flight state changes with bounded call-stack growth while preserving cancellation, ownership, buffered mutation, and final-state behavior.

FR-004.title: Player-action dispatch MUST retain atomic validation, mutation, persistence, revision, and response behavior when decomposed into cohesive phases.

FR-005.title: Terminal activation paths MUST share their common state-transition behavior while preserving route-specific navigation and failure semantics.

FR-006.title: Character value constraints MUST have one canonical domain definition reused at application and control boundaries, while each boundary MUST retain its required presence and trust checks.

FR-007.title: New-session, open-session, and demo-copy commands MUST share common orchestration while preserving each command's labels, inputs, side effects, and errors.

FR-008.title: Extracted-update manifest validation MUST be separated into focused validation stages while preserving every existing rejection rule and diagnostic category.

FR-009.title: Cohesive source concerns MAY be moved into feature-focused files within their existing packages, but package ownership, exported interfaces, initialization behavior, and generated files MUST remain unchanged.

FR-010.title: Refactoring MUST preserve all established user-visible behavior, persisted data compatibility, public/private boundaries, and concurrency guarantees.

FR-011.title: All changed Go code MUST follow the repository's Go quality and simplification guidance, including clarity, minimal interfaces, explicit error context, dependency discipline, and removal of redundant state or helpers.

FR-012.title: Every changed Go test MUST register test-owned resource cleanup immediately with test cleanup hooks; cleanup requiring a context MUST use a cancellation-independent bounded context, while lexical cleanup MAY continue to use function-scoped deferral.

FR-013.title: The completed change MUST pass formatting, static analysis, unit tests, and race-enabled tests applicable to the affected runtime paths.

FR-014.title: Repository-wide macOS Go validation uses the governed deployment environment without linker target-version warnings.

intent: Simplify and harden the Go codebase while preserving runtime behavior, contracts, and concurrency guarantees.
context: area: application, control, domain, live, session, tunnel, and update packages
constraint: Google Go Style Guide plus repository Go quality and simplification skills
constraint: test-owned cleanup uses t.Cleanup with cancellation-independent bounded cleanup contexts

No schema, RPC, generated-file, persistence-format, or package-boundary changes.

approach: Add focused regressions, centralize domain copy and validation rules, convert recursive lifecycle waits to loops, and extract transaction-local orchestration helpers without changing package or contract ownership.

decisions.decision: Use the domain package as canonical content-node copy owner.
decisions.why: It already has the complete copy semantics and prevents service-specific field omissions.

decisions.decision: Use sentinel error identities with wrapping for control failure classification.
decisions.why: errors.Is provides stable machine classification without changing transport contracts.
decisions.rejected: Parse human-readable error strings or add schema codes.

decisions.decision: Represent lifecycle retries as lock-releasing loops.
decisions.why: Loops preserve the state machine while bounding call-stack growth.
decisions.rejected: Recursive re-entry or a new coordinator goroutine.

decisions.decision: Keep player-action decomposition inside one existing commit boundary.
decisions.why: Helpers reduce branching while preserving transaction and effect ordering.
decisions.rejected: New service interfaces or separate commits.

decisions.decision: Preserve exact invalid-durable-state diagnostics with an identity-carrying wrapper.
decisions.why: Application classification needs a stable persistence identity while control tests and maintainers retain the more specific diagnostic.
decisions.rejected: Replace every persistence diagnostic with one generic error string.

decisions.decision: Use interface method expressions for shared session command orchestration.
decisions.why: They preserve the three distinct callbacks without closure boilerplate or a new command enum.
decisions.rejected: Keep three duplicated facade bodies or introduce a command registry.
